reviews.text: The makers of the app recently changed the subscription tiers. I’d been a paid subscriber for years but suddenly they made it so that I would have to pay over $100 more per year to continue using the app the way I had been. They actually limited the number of custom maps (that I make) that can be imported into the app. It’s basically useless to me now.

reviews.title: This app no longer works
reviews.text: I used this app for many years and have bought hundreds of dollars of maps. But over time I have lost access to almost all of them. I carried on using the app regardless - buying new maps to replace old ones that had disappeared. But today on buying a map the app took my money and then simply displayed an interminable error message. The process to request a refund is itself a nightmare, requiring you to answer many many irrelevant questions and then go through an email verification process - even if you’re already signed in to the app with that email address. It’s a death by many cuts but today’s problems have ruined a day of hiking holiday and make me realize I just need to go back to buying maps on paper, such is the creeping encrapification of Avenzanmals.

reviews.title: Removed custom maps from Free account
reviews.text:
I’ve been using custom maps in Avenza for years. I only need them a few times a year, but when I do, it was always incredibly helpful. They’ve now removed the ability to import your own which, while something I need, is not worth $35 a year in subscription fees. I’m now looking for another solution.

Update: even paying for the plus subscription only lets you import 20 maps in perpetuity! If you import the wrong map or a single multipage pdf, your subscription becomes useless! Even if you delete the maps you loaded, new slots do not open up unless you shell out $170/yr. Predatory and scummy, I hope Avenza’s new owners lose a ton of money with these new policies.

reviews.title: Map limit bad for backpacking
reviews.text: The new subscription structure is really hostile. I actually paid because I don’t mind supporting the application a bit. However, the limit to maps you can import is 10. This is completely arbitrary and hostile  to users. The problem is that hikers who prepare maps in Garmin or CalTopo typically have a few pages of maps in a pdf and these all count as separate maps. You can’t import a pdf with more than 10 pages of maps now. Remove this ridiculous limit and maybe people would actually be willing to pay.

reviews.title: Do not trust Avenza for long term!
reviews.text: I used Avenza maps for multiple  elk and mule deer hunts. Loved the interface very clean tracks and waypoints. BUT!!! I saved vital tracks in, glassing spots, access around pinnacles and bluffs. Days and days of vital information for return trips. All was good for about 5 years. I went to open a map for a Nevada mule deer hunt I drew again but it would not open. When that wouldn’t open I tried all of my maps, none would open.I contacted Avenza and they told me they lost licensing for the maps which is a very common occurrence. Not only would the maps not open, I could not retrieve any of the data as in tracks and waypoints as they were only saved to that map. Very disappointed. Like I said I love the interface but I cannot trust Avenza with anything long term.

reviews.title: Off-line mapping pro premium plus, now with more payment options.
reviews.text: I’ve had this app for at least five years now, as a reliable off-line map for the local area or downloading a portion for hikes and adventures. I loved that it was no nonsense, three free offline maps which was enough for me. Now the maps that I would help fellow hikers or bikers with have been blocked by yet another paywall. If the maps I rely on can be screwed over by changing the payment method I have no reason to trust the app. Please revert the offline system or expect to drift away like a fart on the wind.

reviews.title: Update reduces functionality again…
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app for years, upgraded to Plus as I needed to store more maps. Everyone I work and adventure with has a Plus account at this point. After the most recent update a Pro account is now required to share maps, which was an unpleasant surprise after several years of sending maps back and forth at job sites, trailheads, etc. usually in spotty cell reception. After all the aggravating cute little updates over the years, I can’t decide if this is the final straw or not.
